I couldn't find the "right" way to do it, but if there's anyone else on the internet who wants to use VIM as a distraction free writer, here's how I did it.

1) Go to your home directory and make a new directory called .vim

2) Go to .vim and make another directory in it called colors

3) in ~/.vim/colors make a file called writing.vim (or whatever you want to call your colorscheme so long as it ends in .vim)

4) put this in there:

set background=dark
highlight clear
if exists("syntax_on")
 syntax reset
endif
let g:colors_name ="Writing"
highlight Normal ctermbg=black ctermfg=green
highlight EndOfBuffer ctermfg=black ctermbg=black

5) now go back to ~/ and make a file called .vimrc

6) put this in there:

syntax on

highlight EndOfBuffer ctermfg=black ctermbg=black

let s:hidden_all = 0
function! ToggleHiddenAll()
 if s:hidden_all == 0
 let s:hidden_all = 1
 set noshowmode
 set noruler
 set laststatus=0
 set noshowcmd
 else
 let s:hidden_all = 0
 set showmode
 set ruler
 set laststatus=2
 set showcmd
 endif
endfunction

nnoremap <S-h> :call ToggleHiddenAll()<CR>

that lets you hide the status bar stuff with "shift-h" in normal mode.

7) To get the "padding" install tmux

8) in ~/ make the file .tmux.conf

9) put this in there:

TERM=screen-256color
set -g status off
set-option -g pane-border-fg black
set-option -g pane-active-border-fg black

10) To enjoy distraction free writing in VIM start tmux, split the screen vertically (CTRL-b then SHIFT-5) and then split the screen horizontally (CTRL-b then "). Then, open VIM in each of the windows, hide everything with SHIFT-H, and work in the panel in the middle.
